Article Title: 'Lotus has withered': Akhilesh Yadav's swipe at BJP over 'Radhe Radhe Kamal Khila De' slogan
Article Text:
"Schools that have been shut down will be reopened": Akhilesh Yadav ahead of UP Assembly elections 2027

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: Taking a swipe at the BJP over its “Radhe Radhe Kamal Khila De” slogan for the upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav said on Sunday that the slogan itself indicated that the ruling party’s "kamal" (lotus symbol) had withered and needed to bloom once again."'Radhe Radhe Kamal Khila De' go ahead and make it bloom. Does it mean the lotus has withered? Why do you (BJP) need to make it bloom again? It has withered," the former Uttar Pradesh chief minister told reporters at a press conference in Lucknow.Akhilesh Yadav also accused the BJP of selectively invoking religious sentiments, clarifying that his party had no objection to religious discourses or 'kathas' but opposed controversial remarks about Hindu deities."The Samajwadi Party is not against 'katha'. But what were the views expressed about the father of Lord Shri Ram, and what was said about Lord Krishna? These are the same BJP people who once made Lord Hanuman dance at their programme," he said, without naming anyone."Can anyone make such remarks about Lord Ram's father? Tell me, what would happen if someone from among us made a similar statement?" he added.Although the SP chief did not name anyone, his remarks appeared to be directed at preacher Dhirendra Krishna Shastri, who recently courted controversy over statements concerning Lord Ram and Lord Krishna.Akhilesh Yadav also hit back at Uttar Pradesh deputy chief minister and BJP leader Keshav Prasad Maurya over his remarks that SP leaders, who once hesitated to chant "Jai Shri Ram", were now uncomfortable with the slogan "Radhe Radhe".Responding to Maurya's comments, Akhilesh Yadav said, "I would never invite him (Maurya) to my house in my lifetime. But you are welcome to visit our house; we will greet you with 'Radhe Radhe'," he told a reporter.The Uttar Pradesh assembly elections are scheduled to take place in February-March next year. The BJP will be aiming for a third consecutive term in power, while Akhilesh Yadav will look to become chief minister for a second time, having last held the post from 2012 to 2017.
Article Summary: Akhilesh Yadav takes a swipe at the BJP over its “Radhe Radhe Kamal Khila De’ slogan for the upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. He says the slogan itself indicated that the ruling party’s "kamal" (lotus symbol) had withered and needed to bloom once again.

Article Title: 'Uncouth, greedy, casteist male chauvinists’: Rahul shares Ardhanareshwar image to target BJP-RSS
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Sunday upped the ante against BJP and RSS , calling them "uncouth, greedy, casteist male chauvinists" and accusing them of having no understanding of India's spiritual and religious traditions."The deeper I go into Indian spiritual and religious traditions, the clearer it becomes," the Congress leader wrote in a social media post on X."The BJP and RSS are uncouth, greedy, casteist male chauvinists with absolutely no understanding of our spiritual and religious traditions," he added.The Congress leader also shared a picture of a sculpture depicting Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati in the form of 'Ardhanareshwar'. Ardhanareshwar is a Hindu deity representing Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati in a single form, with one half depicting a male and the other a female.Rahul's remarks come days after he faced criticism over his comments about his parents' relationship at the launch of his mother Sonia Gandhi 's memoir, 'Belonging: A Journey Of Love'.Recalling his childhood, he said his parents would sit together during meals, with his mother sitting on his father's lap."Now, I thought this was a normal thing. So I would go to my friend's house, but their parents wouldn't be sitting on each other's lap, and I'd ask my friends, 'Guys, what is going on? Why is your mother not sitting on your father's lap?'" he said."... And then we saw it all get smashed. Not just over time - suddenly... We saw one of our anchors (Indira Gandhi) get shot, and then we saw our biggest anchor (Rajiv) get blown to pieces," he added.The remarks drew criticism from BJP leaders, including Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, who took a swipe at the Congress leader."Sorry, Ma'am, he couldn't spare you the embarrassment even on such a special day of your life. The nation figured it out long ago. Hopefully you'll see it now too; this product is beyond launching and relaunching," Sarma said in a post on X, sharing a video of Rahul's remarks.The Congress leader countered saying thar fear, anger and hatred had created a web in the hearts of BJP and RSS supporters, preventing them from expressing love.He had also shared a photograph of a 12th-century temple sculpture depicting Goddess Parvati sitting on Lord Shiva's lap."As a true Hindu, it is my duty to free them from this web, so that they too can start to experience the breathtaking beauty and joy of love and belonging in their lives. Satyam Shivam Sundaram," he had said.Congress had backed Rahul's remarks, saying the Lok Sabha leader of opposition had initiated a much-needed conversation."...Love need not be hidden, affection is not a weakness, and equality begins with treating your partner as an equal," the party had said in a post on X, tagging Rahul's remarks.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi calls BJP and RSS "uncouth, greedy, casteist male chauvinists" He accuses them of having no understanding of India's spiritual and religious traditions. His remarks come days after he faced criticism over his comments about his parents' relationship.

Article Title: 'This is new India's response': BJP takes swipe at Pakistan over its minister's applause at Purana Qila
Article Text:
It highlighted the contrast between the remarks and the Pakistani minister's presence at an event showcasing India's cultural heritage.

The BJP on Sunday took a swipe at Pakistan by sharing a video of Pakistan minister Musadik Malik applauding during the event at the Purana Qila. They shared the moment of Malik applauding at a presentation on Indian civilisation, Kashmir 's culture and the Mahabharata and used it to get back at Pakistan's earlier remarks on Kashmir and India.BJP's national account shared a video montage of Pakistani leaders' statements on Kashmir featuring army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir and Musadik Malik. Their words are later juxtaposed with visuals of Malik and other delegates applauding at the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum.The video, edited with the track 'Ari Ari' from Dhurandhar as the background music, was posted by the BJP's national account. It juxtaposed clips of statements about Kashmir, India's water resources and Hindus.It highlighted the contrast between the remarks and the Pakistani minister's presence at an event showcasing India's cultural heritage."Those who lay claim to Kashmir, threaten to break up India and insult Hindus… were applauding India’s civilisation, Kashmir’s culture and the epic of the Mahabharata at the Purana Qila!" the BJP said in its post, adding, "This is the new India’s response!"The video carried captions highlighting remarks such as "Kashmir belongs to Pakistan", "We will cut hands of those who block our water" and "We are different from Hindus.Hindus are inferior". It then showed Malik and other attendees applauding during cultural presentations.The BJP also used captions to underline its political message. One read, "Those who claim Kashmir are applauding when Kashmiri culture is presented as Indian". Another said, "Those who threatened to cut India's hands were left clapping for India".The three-day SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum is being hosted by India at the historic Purana Qila. Malik, Pakistan's minister for climate change and environmental coordination, was among the delegates attending the event.During his address at the forum, Malik had invoked Mughal emperor Humayun and Sher Shah Suri, both associated with the construction of Purana Qila. He described the historic fortress as a reflection of multiple layers of history.
Article Summary: BJP's national account shared a video montage of Pakistani leaders' statements on Kashmir featuring army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir and Musadik Malik. Their words are later juxtaposed with visuals of Malik and other delegates applauding at the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum.

Article Title: 'Main chunauti ko chunauti diye bina reh nahi sakta’: PM Modi at IIT Kharagpur’s 75th anniversary

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday said he cannot let a challenge go unchallenged, highlighting his approach towards overcoming difficulties while addressing the Platinum Jubilee celebrations of IIT Kharagpur in West Bengal."Mere swabhaav mein hi bana hain ki main chunauti ko chunauti diye bina reh nahi sakta hoon," Modi said, emphasising his determination to confront challenges.Recalling the history of IIT Kharagpur, the Prime Minister said the institution stands on a site that once served as a detention camp for freedom fighters, adding that their legacy continues to inspire generations of students"The land of Bengal is a place that has nurtured ideas and served as a cradle for national movements. This very institution stands on a site that once served as a detention camp for freedom fighters. Just imagine—what might the freedom fighters who were held in this detention camp have discussed, or what might they have thought about throughout the day? The atmosphere here still resonates with the echoes of their lives, their thoughts, and their activities from that era—serving as a guiding mantra that continues to inspire you all today," he said. PM Modi said the detention camps had witnessed the courage and determination of Indians who fought for self-rule and envisioned India reaching great heights."Decades ago, these very detention camps witnessed the indomitable spirit and courage of those Indians who yearned for self-rule and envisioned India reaching great heights. And today, on this same land, stands our IIT—transformed and revitalised—where young minds are being nurtured, whose innovations and ideas are becoming the driving force behind making India self-reliant," he said.During the celebrations, the Prime Minister also unveiled a special commemorative coin marking 75 years of IIT Kharagpur.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi said he cannot let a challenge go unchallenged. He was addressing the Platinum Jubilee celebrations of IIT Kharagpur in West Bengal. PM Modi said the institution stands on a site that once served as a detention camp for freedom fighters.

Article Title: Reflecting on Purana Qila's history, Pakistan minister invokes Humanyun & Sher Shah Suri at SCO civilisational dialogue to assert cultural diversity
Article Text:
The remarks come amid strained India-Pakistan relations following the 2025 Pahalgam terror attack. Malik is visiting India for the first time.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Venue of the first civilisational dialogue under the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Forum, Purana Qila symbolised civilisational continuity but in the case of Pakistan with a different perspective. In marked contrast to India, which It’s minister Musadik Masood Malik on Saturday chose to emphasise that the foundations of the Old Fort were laid by Humanyun whose origins lay in central Asia and that its construction was carried forward by Sher Shah Suri who came from Afghanistan as he sought to focus on the sub continent’s cultural diversity.“Its foundation was laid by Humayun, who belonged to the Timurid dynasty and had arrived from Central Asia. Its construction was further carried forward by Sher Shah Suri, who came from Afghanistan. Thus, within a single wall, one could find the art of two different rulers, two cultural layers, and traces of two traditions,” Malik said.India has touted Old Fort as the perfect venue for the meet with its multi-layered history and its identity as the ancient city of Indraprastha mentioned in the epic ‘Mahabharata’. As part of the retelling of the approximately 3000-year long history of the site, India showcased nine layers of continuity--among them the standing ramparts built by Sher Shah Suri (1538-1545 CE) after demolishing and re-modeling Dinpanah, a city founded here by Humayun, around 1533 CE.Reflecting on the excavations at the site, Malik said, “Delhi has not been diminished by civilisations and people coming from outside; rather, it has grown stronger”.During his inaugural speech on Friday Prime Minister Narendra Modi had also reflected on the history of Purana Qila to assert India’s civilisational journey going back thousands of years to the Mahabharata period. He also visited the ‘Mahabharata Pavillion - Anant: A rare 18th century Mahabharata scroll’ and the exhibition ‘Astitva’ offering an immersive account of Delhi’s history through archaeological evidence, that have been curated for the leaders from SCO countries to see.Day two of the Fourm saw ministers of all participating nations make statements. Malik who happens to be the Climate Change and Environmental Coordination referring to archaeological remains from different periods discovered during excavations at Purana Qila, said that the fort in which the delegates were seated was, in itself, a story. He appreciated the description of the event as ‘Tehzeeb Ki Guftagu’, or ‘Dialogue of Civilisations’.
Article Summary: India has touted Old Fort as the perfect venue for the meet with its multi- layered history and its identity as the ancient city of Indraprastha mentioned in the epic ‘Mahabharata’ The remarks come amid strained India-Pakistan relations following the 2025 Pahalgam terror attack.

Article Title: Over 10k postgraduate medical seats in blocked category; govt may review float system
Article Text:
As per data, 10,105 seats were listed under the ‘Blocking’ category after Round 2 of NEET-PG 2026 counselling

NEW DELHI: More than 10,000 postgraduate medical seats were listed under the blocked category after Round 2 of NEET-PG 2026 counselling, with the data indicating that some candidates were holding one seat through All India counselling and another through state counselling simultaneously, prompting the govt to consider changes to the newly introduced float system.According to the SARTHA app, a medical admission and counselling platform for NEET-PG and NEET-UG aspirants, 10,105 seats were listed under the 'Blocking' category after Round 2 of NEET-PG 2026 counselling. The app, filtered for MCC (All India) counselling, describes these as seats held by students who also have an allotment in another counselling process. The data was shared by Dr Kapil Dev on social media.The branch-wise breakup showed MD General Medicine accounting for the highest number of blocked seats at 1,026, followed by MS Obstetrics and Gynaecology (861) and MS General Surgery (786), according to the app. Dr Nachiket Bhatia, a medico-socio activist, has also flagged the issue on his social media account.A senior official familiar with the counselling process said the float facility, which allows candidates to retain an allotted seat while seeking an upgrade, could be contributing to dual seat blocking as all-India and state counselling run parallelly on separate platforms. "A candidate may opt for float in both processes and end up blocking two seats," the official said.Introduced for students' convenience, the facility allows candidates to retain seats while seeking an upgrade, with physical joining becoming compulsory in the third round. The official said govt may consider restricting float to the first round and making physical joining compulsory from the second round in future counselling cycles. "This is the first time we have introduced the float system in this manner.We will analyse the situation after the third round."The official also flagged the absence of a common counselling platform linking all-India and state processes, which run simultaneously on separate portals, making it difficult to track candidates holding seats in both. A common portal could prevent multiple allotments, but differences in state reservation policies and concerns over loss of control have hindered integration.Meanwhile, Federation of All India Medical Association has sought a 24-hour deferment of NEET-PG Round 2 results and a one-day window for eligible candidates to surrender either their All India or state quota seats.
Article Summary: 10,105 seats were listed under the ‘Blocking’ category after Round 2 of NEET-PG 2026 counselling. Data indicated that some candidates were holding one seat through All India counselling and another through state counselling simultaneously. MD General Medicine accounting for the highest number of blocked seats at 1,026.

NEW DELHI: The selection of India's playing XI has triggered a face-off between the Congress and the BJP, with the opposition alleging discrimination against pacer Mohammed Siraj and the ruling party accusing it of dragging communal politics into cricket.The exchange began after India’s team management opted for a four-pronged pace attack but left out Siraj against New Zealand, despite the Hyderabad pacer’s impressive record and reputation for delivering in challenging conditions.Congress MP Imran Masood questioned Siraj’s exclusion, suggesting that his religious identity could have played a role in the decision."His name is Siraj -- isn't that reason enough? If he is performing and still not getting selected, what else could be the reason behind it? This alone can be the reason; there can be no other reason besides this," Masood told news agency IANS.In another interaction, the Congress MP said it was being pointed out that Siraj had performed well but was still not included in the team. "If you are not selecting him despite his good performance, the discrimination is clear," he told news agency ANI.The BJP was quick to hit back, accusing the Congress of turning team selection into a communal issue and using cricket for vote-bank politics.BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari said, "Shame on Congress! Congress now does vote bank politics even in Cricket team selection! Congress says - 'Siraj was left out because he was a Muslim'."Pointing out that all-rounder Ravindra Jadeja had also been left out, Bhandari said, "Every cricketer wears the jersey representing India! Stop dividing Indian cricket team for vote bank and communal politics!"Siraj's omission has also drawn attention because of the role he has played in India's pace attack over the past few years.Fifteen months ago, on a cloudy morning in London, Siraj stepped out of Jasprit Bumrah's shadow to produce one of the most memorable performances of his career. The pacer emptied the tank on the final day of a gruelling five-Test series to help India secure a 2-2 draw against England at The Oval.His performance appeared to signal the beginning of a new phase in his career, with Siraj emerging as a potential leader of India's pace attack as Bumrah entered an intensive workload management programme.However, the pacer was left out on Thursday despite conditions in Wellington appearing tailor-made for seam bowling. The team management instead went ahead with four other seamers.One possible reason for the decision could be Siraj's recent form. His underwhelming performance against Sri Lanka in the Colombo Test three months ago may have prompted the team management to reassess his place in the playing XI.
Article Summary: Mohammed Siraj left out of India's pace attack against New Zealand. Congress alleges discrimination, BJP says stop dividing team for vote bank and communal politics. India's team management opted for a four-pronged pace attack but left out Siraj.

Article Title: Humayun, Sher Shah and ‘one fort’: Pakistan minister highlights Purana Quila’s layered history at SCO forum
Article Text:
The remarks come amid strained India-Pakistan relations following the 2025 Pahalgam terror attack. Malik is visiting India for the first time.

Three-day SCO civilisational forum at Purana Quila

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Pakistan minister Musadik Malik invoked Mughal emperor Humayun and Afghan ruler Sher Shah Suri while addressing the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum at Delhi's historic Purana Quila on Saturday. Referring to the fort's layered history, Malik said it reflected how two rival rulers had contributed to the construction of the same monument.Speaking at the thematic session titled 'Civilisational and Cultural Expressions', chaired by Union culture minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Malik described Purana Quila as a symbol of multiple historical influences."This (Purana) Quila, where we are sitting, is in itself a story. A fort, whose foundation was laid by Humayun, who had a descent from the Timurid (dynasty) linkage.. came from Central Asia. And Sher Shah Suri further built on it, who was an Afghan. One wall, two rivals, meaning two rulers and one fort, meaning two layers and one trench," the Pakistan minister said.Malik also shared a video of his address on X and wrote in Urdu that the Quila is a "story".He further emphasised the importance of dialogue between different identities and cultures, saying, "dialogue is between distinct identities, and between diversity, and, we have come here for that dialogue only"."Meaning, many voices, many identities, and their dialogues, and free flow of ideas, among them... free flow of identities. The wisdom lies in it, the wisdom lies in embracing it, embellishing it. So, wisdom is there in it, and needs courage too. And, we have gathered here to celebrate these two things," he added.The remarks come amid strained India-Pakistan relations following the 2025 Pahalgam terror attack. Malik is visiting India for the first time.India is hosting the three-day SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum at Purana Quila to highlight the country's rich civilisational heritage and the layers of history spanning thousands of years.Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the summit on Friday evening in the presence of delegates from SCO member countries, including Malik.The choice of venue also draws attention to the fort's historical significance. Humayun, the second Mughal emperor, laid its foundation, while Sher Shah Suri later expanded it. Humayun's Tomb, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Delhi's Nizamuddin area, is also located nearby.The tomb is the first garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent. It marked a major departure from earlier funerary traditions and is considered a pioneering example of Indo-Islamic architecture, according to the culture ministry.As part of the forum, a special exhibition titled 'Astitva: The Essence of our Existence' has been organised for SCO delegates. It offers an account of Delhi's history through archaeological evidence dating from 1,200 BC to 1200 CE. The exhibition includes excavated remains, artefacts, architectural fragments and other significant discoveries.
Article Summary: Pakistan minister Musadik Malik is visiting India for the first time. He is addressing the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum at Delhi's historic Purana Quila. The remarks come amid strained India- Pakistan relations following the 2025 Pahalgam terror attack.

Article Title: 'No place for hate in cricket’: Congress leader rejects Masood’s religious bias charge over Siraj
Article Text:
Congress leader rejects Masood’s religious bias charge over Siraj

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Mumtaz Patel has rejected party colleague Imran Masood's allegation of religious discrimination in the selection of the Indian cricket team, saying players have always been picked on the basis of form and suitability rather than religion, caste or region.Patel's remarks came after Masood alleged that fast bowler Mohammed Siraj was left out of India's playing eleven for the first Test against New Zealand because of his religious identity. Speaking to news agency ANI, Patel said cricket should remain separate from the communal divisions seen in political discourse."In cricket as a sport, I think there is no space for hate or this religious divide. Firstly, when we talk about Team India, I think the most prominent thing in that is India, and we've always seen cricket in its highest form. I would say that this religious divide, hate divide, is not acceptable," she said.Patel maintained that team selections were based on players' performances and the requirements of a particular tournament."I think cricketers with the best form, best suited in that particular tournament as a team, have always been put together. I doubt I have never seen cricket being divided in the name of states, religion, culture, caste or anything.Let's keep this away," she said.She also criticised political messaging that, in her view, contributed to an atmosphere of division, referring to campaign slogans and remarks by leaders without naming them."At the same time I want to say that let's not create this atmosphere of hate and divide in our country. When you have top leaders on stage talking about people being identified by their clothes, or leaders saying 'batenge toh katenge', it creates a negative atmosphere in the country. Let's keep all this separate. Let's be a united India and especially when it comes to cricket, we are united as Team India," Patel added.Earlier on Saturday, Congress Rajya Sabha MP Ranjeet Ranjan had also urged Masood to keep politics and sports separate, saying athletes should not be drawn into political discourse."...I would simply urge Masood-ji to keep politics and sports separate; please, let us not interfere in sports. Sports has its own domain, its own criteria for merit, and every player has their own unique struggle. I strongly believe that while we may engage in political manoeuvring, we should not drag sports or athletes into our political discourse. I find that completely unacceptable..," Ranjan said.The controversy began on Friday after Masood questioned Siraj's omission from the playing eleven, alleging that the decision was linked to his name and religion."It is being said that despite his good performance, he was not given a place in the team. His name is 'Siraj', and that is why he was not given a place. If you are not selecting him despite his good performance, the discrimination is clear," Masood told ANI.On Saturday, Masood cited fast bowler Mohammed Shami and batter Sarfaraz Khan while questioning the selection process."There's Mohammed Shami, there's Sarfaraz, and many others. Selections should be based on performance; if someone is performing well, it shouldn't matter where they come from," he said.Questions over Siraj's omission have also drawn attention to his record in the ongoing World Test Championship cycle. He has taken 43 wickets in 11 matches, according to the information cited in the reports.India selected Jasprit Bumrah, Prasidh Krishna, Akash Deep and Anshul Kamboj as its four pacers for the Test, alongside Washington Sundar. The team management cited its bowling combination and the need for additional batting cover.
Article Summary: Congress leader Mumtaz Patel rejects Imran Masood's allegation of religious discrimination in selection of Indian cricket team. Patel says players have always been picked on the basis of form and suitability rather than religion, caste or region. Masood alleged that fast bowler Mohammed Siraj was left out of India's playing eleven for the first Test against New Zealand because of his religious identity.

NEW DELHI: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) will contest all 70 constituencies in the upcoming Uttarakhand Assembly elections, ruling out an alliance with any political party for now.Addressing a press conference in Dehradun, Sisodia said the decision was taken after consultations with AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal and other senior party leaders."It has been decided that we will strongly contest all 70 seats," Sisodia said, ANI reported.She said Kejriwal had given the state leadership the go-ahead to begin preparations in full swing and assured that he would visit Dehradun and constituencies where the party has a strong organisational presence. Article Title: In joy & grief, high airfares keep Indian families apart
Article Text:
High airfares are forcing Indians living away from home to miss weddings, festivals and family milestones, turning visits into a luxury.

Airfares as of Nov 1. Fares are dynamic and subject to change

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NOIDA: Ananya will miss her BFF’s wedding. Riya marked her presence at her grandmother’s 97th birthday on a video call. Aditi could not be home for ‘bhai phota’. Kavya watched from afar her family’s celebrations on the birth of her niece. Vasant grieved quietly as his uncle breathed his last at home thousands of kilometres away.Migration defines the working Indian, and many who have moved to Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad and other economic hubs fly home multiple times a year to make sure they remain present, in joy or in grief, next to loved ones.This year, exorbitant airfares are coming in the way, reports Ayantika Pal. Aditi, who studies clinical psychology in Delhi, abandoned her decision to fly home to Kolkata during the Nov 6-15 Diwali break, mainly for ‘bhai phota’ (bhai dooj). “The starting fare was Rs 23,000 for a round trip,” she says.“My brother has been my constant support system after our father’s death. This is a special occasion. I’ve never missed a bhai phota,” says Aditi. She understands it’s an expense her family can’t afford. “I couldn’t go during Durga Puja either. My entire festive season was spent within the four walls of my PG room,” she says.For students and early-career professionals, limited leave and incomes anyway make short-notice decisions to fly expensive.But thanks to the way airfares have risen this year, with airlines citing higher fuel costs because of the Iran war, such decisions have become unaffordable. Especially around festivals and the wedding season, a short visit can wipe out much of a month’s earnings. Trains aren’t an alternative for a brief visit. “Train tickets are never available at short notice anyway,” Aditi says.Festive-season fares reached Supreme Court on Nov 2 when it refused an urgent hearing on a plea seeking a cap on domestic airfares. The petitioner alleged fares had surged as much as 700% on some routes. Justice Vikram Nath told counsel, who argued air travel was essential: “Don’t travel by air.”For 23-year-old Ananya Nair, a media professional living in a rented flat in Noida, her best friend’s wedding in Kerala on Dec 6 will be something she follows on Instagram. The cheapest direct morning flight to Kochi from Delhi that weekend is Rs 17,000. For a round trip, the flight spend is upwards of Rs 30,000, not counting seat and meal expenses and cab fares. “How am I supposed to afford this?” she says. “We had promised to stand beside each other at our weddings. ”Kavya (23), a Delhi-based professional from Sriperumbudur near Chennai, missed the naming ceremony of her niece born in July. She hopes to save enough to visit in Jan, when the baby will be six months old. “She is already four months old, but I haven’t even held her in my arms yet. I’ve become an aunt for the first time!” Kavya says. “These first few months will never come back, and it breaks my heart that I am missing them simply because I cannot afford to go home. The cheapest one-way fare I found was Rs 11,800. That was beyond me,” she said.For Riya Sharma (26), a Gurgaon-based beauty salon professional, the cost of flying to Jabalpur and back was more than 50% of her monthly paycheck. “The cheapest flight, via Hyderabad, was Rs 8,000 but that meant a long detour and flying time of over seven hours. I watched my grandmother cut the cake with my family over a video call. Visiting family now feels like a luxury,” she says.For Vasant, the last few weeks were tough. His uncle, suddenly diagnosed with a clot in the brain, needed immediate surgery. “In hospital, a heart problem was detected as well. He had to undergo two surgeries before he passed away. My family back home in Bhubaneswar was there, as were some of my childhood friends. I couldn’t go because the round-trip flight fares were almost Rs 27,000,” he said.In the upcoming Christmas and New Year fortnight, more plans are likely to be shelved.A check by TOI on Nov 21 of one-way airfares from Delhi to major destinations for two key holiday dates — Christmas (Dec 25) and New Year’s Day (Jan 1) — revealed steep ticket prices on most routes.Both dates fall on Fridays, offering travellers extended weekends. Ticket prices are the highest in the Delhi-Bengaluru and Delhi-Kolkata sectors and Delhi-Ahmedabad sectors, among the big cities, with the highest ticket price already touching nearly Rs 20,000 for a one-way ticket.Travel agents said fewer flights, especially with Air India pulling out services from several routes as part of its cost-cutting strategy, had brought down seat availability and pushed up fares further. “During the recently concluded Chhath Puja, a one-way flight from Bengaluru to Patna cost as much as Rs 25,000. With trains fully booked and flights becoming unaffordable, some people are resorting to travelling by tempos,” said Ram Kumar of Ghumo India, a Delhi-based travel agency. “Between Dec 25 and Jan 5, we receive bookings from across India for destinations such as Kashmir, Shimla, Manali and Ladakh. Passengers who need to travel on specific dates have little bargaining power.”
Article Summary: High airfares are forcing Indians living away from home to miss weddings, festivals and family milestones, turning visits into a luxury. Supreme Court on Nov 2 refused an urgent hearing on a plea seeking a cap on domesticAirfares. For a round trip, the flight spend is upwards of Rs 30,000, not counting seat and meal expenses and cab fares.

Article Title: ICMR: Common antibiotics losing potency as drug resistance rises
Article Text:
The findings come at a time when govt is drawing attention to the misuse of antibiotics

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Antibiotics used to treat common bacterial infections are increasingly losing their effectiveness, with a new Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) report finding only 18.4% of E. coli samples tested in hospitals were susceptible to cefotaxime, an antibiotic used to treat serious infections such as pneumonia and UTIs.The findings come at a time when govt is drawing attention to the misuse of antibiotics. At the launch of World Antimicrobial Resistance Awareness Week (Nov 18), the health ministry highlighted concerns over antibiotic sales without prescriptions and inappropriate prescribing.ICMR’s Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance and Research Network annual report for 2025 also found high resistance to stronger antibiotics used to treat severe infections. Only around one-third of Klebsiella pneumoniae samples were susceptible to carbapenems, powerful antibiotics often reserved for serious infections that do not respond to other medicines.Another finding was 91.1% of revived Acinetobacter baumannii isolates tested were resistant to carbapenems.This can cause serious hospital-acquired infections, particularly pneumonia and bloodstream infections among critically ill patients.Dr Kamini Walia, head of ICMR’s descriptive research division, said the findings showed antimicrobial resistance was not confined to large referral centres. Citing the secondary-care hospital data, she said ceftriaxone susceptibility in E. coli declined from 39.8% in category I hospitals to 28% in category II and just 11.5% in category III.
Article Summary: Only 18.4% of E. coli samples tested in hospitals were susceptible to cefotaxime, an antibiotic used to treat serious infections such as pneumonia and UTIs. The findings come at a time when govt is drawing attention to the misuse of antibiotics.

NEW DELHI: Former BJP spokesperson and Rise & Fall Season 2 winner Shehzad Poonawalla has said that his decision to quit active politics was not driven by any dislike for the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). He also described his political differences with brother Tehseen Poonawalla as a "battle of principles" rather than a personal conflict.In an interview with news agency ANI, Shehzad reaffirmed his support for Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath and Union home minister Amit Shah. He said he continued to hold the BJP in high regard and pointed to his choice of clothing as a sign of his association with the party."Why did I leave politics? It wasn't because I dislike the BJP; if I disliked them, I wouldn't be walking around wearing their T-shirt," he said.Speaking about his differences with his brother, Shehzad alleged that the issues raised by Tehseen were not in the nation's interest. He also claimed that his brother was aligned with Congress leader Rahul Gandhi 's team."I'm just glad these people weren't around during the time of the Mahabharata; otherwise, they would have claimed that the conflict between the Pandavas and the Kauravas was also just a publicity stunt! Our conflict isn't a personal one; it's a battle over principles.I feel that the issues he raises aren't actually in the nation's interest. In a way, it seems like he's part of Rahul Gandhi's team—much like how Arvind Kejriwal pushed Abhijeet Dipke to the forefront because his own credibility had hit zero," he said.He further contrasted his political loyalties with those of his brother, calling Tehseen a representative of the Congress and describing himself as an open supporter of the BJP's top leadership."Tehseen Poonawalla acts as 'Hamza Mazari' for the Congress. As for me, I'm an openly declared supporter of Modi, Yogi, and Amit Shah. For Uttar Pradesh, the combination of Modi and Yogi is only 'useful.' Yes, I have worked both with Rahul Gandhi and Modiji—and that's precisely why I can say, with my eyes closed, that this country won't see another Prime Minister like Modi-ji for the next 100 years," he said.Explaining his political journey, Shehzad said he had initially planned to remain with the BJP until the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. However, he continued working with the party through several subsequent state elections before deciding to return to the media."I left the Congress and joined the media, where I earned a very good salary as an anchor. Then, in 2021, I joined the BJP, with the intention of staying for about three to four years, until the 2024 elections. Then, there were crucial elections in Haryana, Maharashtra, and Bihar, and by the time those concluded, along with the Bengal elections, two years had passed; I moved on. After that, I decided to step away from politics and return to the media," he said.Shehzad also shared his views on Hindu identity and Hindutva, arguing that everyone living in India should identify as Hindu. He referred to the country as Bharat and Hindustan while explaining his position."Every person in this country is a Hindu, and everyone ought to be a 'Hindutva-vadi'. What else is this country called, besides Bharat? It is also known as Hindustan. And what does that imply? It means that anyone who lives here is a Hindu," he said.Reflecting on his victory in reality show Rise & Fall Season 2, Shehzad said winning the trophy was not his idea of a true political rise. He said he would consider it a bigger achievement if Yogi Adityanath secured another electoral victory in 2027 and Modi returned to power in 2029."Some might say that winning a trophy counts as a rise. For us, a true rise would be if Baba (Yogi Adityanath) wins the election for a third time in 2027, and if Modi-ji wins again in 2029... Shehzad Poonawalla might leave the BJP for financial cause, but the BJP can never truly leave Shehzad Poonawalla," he added.
Article Summary: Former BJP spokesperson Shehzad Poonawalla has said that his decision to quit active politics was not driven by any dislike for the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) He described his political differences with brother Tehseen as a "battle of principles" rather than a personal conflict.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Mahomes also praised the squad for staying together through difficult periods and continuing to work towards their goal. Article Title: "I was sick....": Travis Kelce's dad Ed Kelce's painful career detour began with a health battle he could not ignore
Article Text:
Ed Kelce and Travis Kelce (Getty images)

Ed Kelce's military dreams suffered two painful setbacks

Ed Kelce rebuilt his career in the steel industry

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Long before Travis and Jason Kelce became household names in the NFL , their father, Ed Kelce, had a very different future in mind. He wanted to follow his family's military tradition and serve his country. However, a lingering football injury and an unexpected health battle forced him to abandon that ambition. His journey took an unexpected turn, pushing him towards a career in the steel industry and a life far removed from the military path he once imagined.Ed Kelce's ambition to join the military came from his family background. Several generations before him had served, making military service an important part of his family's history. During an appearance on his sons' New Heights podcast on July 26, 2023, he explained why following that path had mattered so much to him."Everybody in my family prior to me was in the service," Ed said.His plans, however, faced an early setback. An injury from his high school football days had left him with damaged cartilage in his left knee. The Army turned down his application because of the problem. He later considered the Coast Guard as another way to fulfil his ambition.But another obstacle emerged just as he began training. Ed developed symptoms of Crohn's disease, an inflammatory bowel condition that can cause serious digestive problems. He recalled how the illness affected him during basic training, making it difficult to continue."I enlisted in the Coast Guard, and the Crohn’s reared up," Ed said. "I’d never had that before, and I was sick. I went through most of the basic training with some severe gastrointestinal issues. They don’t need sick people in the service; they need people who are ready to perform."The experience brought another major change to his plans. His health problems meant he could not continue the military journey he had worked towards.Instead of allowing those setbacks to define his future, Ed Kelce found another direction. He eventually built a career in Cleveland's steel industry, working in sales and supplying products to manufacturers. It was a demanding line of work, but it gave him the opportunity to build a stable life for his family.Ed also made sure his sons understood what his working life involved. In a February 2023 interview with the Los Angeles Times, he recalled taking Jason and Travis to his workplace."I'd take them there — hard hat, safety glasses, boots, the whole nine yards," he said.He wanted them to see the value of different career paths rather than assume that success came through one particular route.His dedication to providing for his family also extended beyond his regular job. Ed later revealed that he took seasonal work at a candy store during the holidays to earn extra money for Christmas gifts."I had two kids that I was crazy about," he said. "I don't think I'm unique in that."His military ambitions never materialised, but Ed built a different kind of legacy. The career he eventually established helped support the family that raised two future NFL stars.
Article Summary: Ed Kelce wanted to follow his family's military tradition and serve his country. A lingering football injury and an unexpected health battle forced him to abandon that ambition. His journey took an unexpected turn, pushing him towards a career in the steel industry and a life far removed from the military path he once imagined.

Arlington police are investigating, while the medical examiner has yet to determine the official cause of death.Jones addressed the case on radio.‘No record of any incidents at the game, and I just got that information. And so we had no record of an incident, and we’ll obviously be looking into that,’ Jones said.He continued: ‘My understanding is the individual went to the game and didn’t feel good at the game, and then left, and has been hospitalized. But we weren’t aware of any incident that involved a fan at the game.’He also defended the stadium’s security system: ‘Let me make the point of, we really do have quite a - eons above what it was 10, 15 years ago - we have quite a surveillance of what’s going on at every aspect of our game.And so it is really rare if we didn’t know of any incident. We’ve got too many people out there; we have 6,000 workers on game day.’Asked whether the Cowboys would share footage with police, Jones replied: ‘Of course!’Narro’s niece Claudia DeLara told the California Post that her uncle said another fan pushed him.‘He got pushed,’ DeLara said. ‘He fell. And immediately he had bruising and swelling in his abdomen.’His friends ‘knew that he was off’ and asked to see his stomach.‘He wasn’t feeling like his normal self and acting like his normal self and so they made him show them his abdomen just to check to see,’ DeLara told The Post. ‘And they said they could visibly see the bruising and, like, a bulge of blood in his abdomen.’After the game, friends called stadium paramedics. Narro was taken to hospital, underwent several emergency surgeries and died on Wednesday.His family filed a police report Tuesday. Arlington police said: ‘At this time, we are treating this case as a death investigation. The investigation is ongoing.’ Police are reviewing stadium footage. The medical examiner awaits autopsy results. No arrests have been announced.DeLara said he ‘just loved the team.’ Jenkins added that Narro would be alive ‘if it weren’t for this football game.’ ‘I just want it to be clear he was an angel of a man, never hurt anyone, never had anything bad to say about anyone,’ Jenkins said. ‘He was so loved. And I’m so sad he fell victim to such mindless violence.’
Article Summary: Jerry Jones says Dallas Cowboys had no record of incident involving Mario Narro. 36-year-old fan died days after an altercation during the November 15 game against the San Francisco 49ers. Narro’s family believes he was pushed and wants answers. He stayed for the game before seeking medical help and died in hospital on Wednesday.

Chelsea could soon attract two high-profile names from very different worlds. Seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady is reportedly exploring a move into the Premier League club, and he may not be the only new investor. Their potential involvement points to a fresh phase in the club’s ownership story, as Clearlake looks for new financial partners following a major change in its shareholder structure.According to The Guardian, Brady and Spiro are in discussions to invest in Clearlake Capital, which controls Chelsea. Instead, they would become limited partners in the investment firm, giving them a financial interest without direct influence over Chelsea’s decisions.The proposed investments are expected to be much smaller than the existing ownership stakes. The New York-based attorney has represented Musk since 2018 and advised him during his $44 billion purchase of Twitter, now known as X, in 2022.His client list also includes celebrities such as Alec Baldwin, Kim Kardashian and Jay-Z. Spiro helped Baldwin secure an acquittal in 2024 after the actor faced involuntary manslaughter charges following the fatal shooting of cinematographer Halyna Hutchins on the set ofHe is also representing investor Joshua Kushner in a legal dispute involving Uefa and Fifa-related business plans. Alec Bohm has spent much of his career focused on making a name for himself in Major League Baseball. But away from the field, the Philadelphia Phillies third baseman was dealing with a difficult situation involving the people closest to him. Bohm accused his parents of mishandling money earned through his baseball career, leading to a multimillion-dollar lawsuit. After months of legal disagreements, the two sides have now reached a settlement, although neither has disclosed the terms.The case attracted attention because it involved more than a disagreement over money. It raised questions about how Bohm's finances were managed and how a family relationship reached the point of a court battle.Bohm filed a lawsuit against his parents, Daniel and Lisa Bohm, seeking at least $3 million. According to his complaint, they had been handling his financial affairs since 2019 and used several limited liability companies to manage his earnings and assets.Bohm alleged that money was moved from his personal accounts into accounts belonging to these companies. He said the arrangement was supposed to help manage and invest his wealth, but claimed that some of the money was instead used for his parents' personal expenses.The complaint also raised concerns about funds connected to the Alec Bohm Foundation.The situation reportedly came to a head when Bohm asked for financial records, account statements and access to information about his holdings. He claimed that his parents provided limited information and later said they would charge him $50 an hour for managing his affairs.His parents rejected the accusations. They argued that the companies had been created with advice from Bohm's lawyer and financial adviser. They also maintained that he knew about the arrangements and had allowed them to manage his finances while he concentrated on his baseball career.Bohm's career had been moving forward long before the family dispute became public. Born in Omaha, Nebraska, on August 3, 1996, he played college baseball at Wichita State University, where his performances helped him become a highly regarded prospect.The Philadelphia Phillies selected him third overall in the 2018 MLB Draft. He made his major league debut in 2020 and gradually became an important part of the team's lineup. His progress reached another milestone in 2024 when he earned his first All-Star selection.Bohm has also been involved in charitable work through the Alec Bohm Foundation. That connection became part of the legal dispute after his complaint raised questions about money associated with the organisation.The legal fight continued for months, with disagreements over financial records and money held in an attorney's trust account. One issue involved $528,618 transferred into the account, which Bohm sought to have frozen while challenging related proceedings in Florida.The settlement was announced after a scheduled hearing at the Philadelphia Court of Common Pleas did not go ahead. Bohm's attorney, Gary DeVito, confirmed that an agreement had been reached but said its terms would remain confidential. His parents' attorney also confirmed the settlement and declined to comment further.The agreement brings the court battle to a close, but it leaves several questions unanswered. Neither side has explained how the financial issues were resolved or whether the settlement will help repair the family relationship.

Article Title: A California mother sued her school district to change her third-grader’s report card, which said he needed to practice 'respect' after a playground incident, after the board voted 4-0 to keep it

Lawsuit seeks new hearing, corrected report card

A few words on a school report card may seem a small part of a child’s academic journey but for one California mother they have become the center of a legal battle. What started as a disagreement over a teacher’s evaluation of behavior on the playground is now in the courts. The parent says her son’s report card does not accurately reflect the circumstances surrounding his interactions with classmates. Still fighting to get the comments removed or corrected, even after the school board unanimously rejected her appeal.On October 5, Weiwei Luo sued the Palo Alto Unified School District and its Board of Education regarding comments on her son's third-grade report card for the 2025-2026 school year, People reports.The student, identified in court documents as K.L., was a student at Walter Hays Elementary School in Palo Alto. Holly Harrison, his teacher, made a number of observations about his interactions with other children, especially how he responded when he was frustrated.The comments said the student is still learning to deal with disagreements, see other people’s points of view and work with classmates. Another assessment indicated he had to continue to practice respect and collaborating with others.But Luo challenged that the comments provided a full picture of the playground events that informed the teacher's assessment.According to the New York Post, the fight started after a string of incidents between the boy and another student in October 2025, including a game of tag.In one particular case, the child was purported to have made a rude gesture at a classmate after the other student kicked him. Ms Luo said the teacher’s assessment did not take into account the lead-up to her son’s reaction.The Post also said the legal petition admitted that Luo had previously acknowledged that her son had acted inappropriately by sticking out his tongue.But the mother wondered whether the teacher’s written comments really addressed the larger situation or focused on what her son said.It’s important to note that Luo is challenging the narrative behavioral comments, not her child’s academic letter grades or social-emotional scores.On June 25, 2026, People reported that Luo requested to change the school records of her son.The district partially granted her request the following month, saying it would revise a separate comment about his academic progress. But officials refused to change the behavior reports, stating they were the professional observations of the teacher.Luo then appealed to the school board. At a hearing on August 18, the board voted 4-0 against her appeal, saying the comments were supported by evidence and were not misleading in light of the entire report card.Luo also claimed the virtual hearing was unfair, the New York Post reported, saying her lawyer was removed from the meeting and could not participate. The district, however, disputed her claims, saying she was told about the hearing arrangements and did not request a delay.Luo is now asking a Santa Clara County judge to overturn the board’s decision and order the district to correct or delete the challenged statements. Or she wants a new hearing with her lawyer present.She is also seeking reimbursement for eligible legal fees and court costs, reports People.“Student privacy laws prohibit the district from discussing individual educational records,” Superintendent Jason Glass told People. “California has procedures for parents to challenge school records, to appeal decisions and to attach written statements explaining their disagreements,” he said.
Article Summary: Weiwei Luo sued the Palo Alto Unified School District and its Board of Education regarding comments on her son's third-grade report card for the 2025-2026 school year. Teacher Holly Harrison made a number of observations about his interactions with other children, especially how he responded when he was frustrated. Luo challenged that the comments provided a full picture of the playground events that informed the teacher's assessment.

Article Title: Israel government formation: Eisenkot invites Netanyahu's Likud party for coalition talks
Article Text:
Eisenkot has time till early December for now to form the govt

Why is Eisenkot reaching out to Netanyahu's party?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

When will Israel get its next government?

Gadi Eisenkot, the former Israeli military chief tasked with forming the country's next government, has invited Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu 's right-wing Likud party for fresh coalition talks, in a move that could pave the way for a national unity government. The talks are scheduled to begin on Sunday, November 22, as Eisenkot faces a December deadline to secure enough support in parliament to replace Netanyahu.Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party said the invitation reflected a "genuine commitment to forming the broadest possible government", as quoted by AFP. The party's negotiating team has been asked to hold a marathon round of discussions with Likud representatives in an effort to break the deadlock over government formation."In an effort to pursue every option for forming a new government, Yashar Chair Gadi Eisenkot has instructed the party's negotiating team to invite its Likud counterparts to a marathon series of talks beginning with the meeting already scheduled for tomorrow (Sunday)," the Yashar party further said in a statement."Leave no stone unturned as it works to make bold moves possible and secure the breakthrough needed to form a government," it added.The two sides had previously held an initial round of talks last Sunday but failed to make progress, with both accusing each other of lacking commitment to a unity government. Likud has demanded that Eisenkot's bloc suspend its legislative agenda and end cooperation with Arab parties.The move comes despite Eisenkot leading a broad anti-Netanyahu political camp. However, the October election left neither the Netanyahu-led right-wing bloc nor the opposition with a clear majority, forcing rival political groups to explore alliances to form the next government.The invitation is significant because Eisenkot has repeatedly ruled out serving in a government led by Netanyahu. However, he had in the past indicated that he would be willing to include members of Likud in a coalition, provided he himself becomes prime minister. The proposed arrangement, if agreed upon would therefore bring Netanyahu's party into government without retaining Netanyahu as its head.The political camp backing Eisenkot is itself divided over how to reach the required parliamentary majority. One option is to bring the ultra-Orthodox parties, Shas and United Torah Judaism, into the coalition. Another is to form a minority government with the backing of Arab-majority parties, including Ra'am and the Joint List. A third option is a national unity government involving Likud.The October 27 election produced a fractured parliament, with no political bloc securing the 61 seats needed for a majority in Israel's 120-member Knesset.Netanyahu's right-wing bloc secured 53 seats, while the opposition bloc led by Eisenkot won 48. Arab-majority parties secured another 19 seats, leaving them potentially important to government formation.Likud emerged as the largest party with 27 seats, followed by Eisenkot's Yashar with 21. Naftali Bennett's B'Yachad won 12 seats.The results has made it difficult for either side to form a government without reaching across political divides, as the required majority is 61.Meanwhile, former prime minister Naftali Bennett, a key figure in Eisenkot's opposition camp, has backed the idea of a national unity government led by Eisenkot, even if it includes Likud.However, he has made clear that he will not serve under Netanyahu. "I am committed to ensuring that Netanyahu will not be the next Prime Minister of the State of Israel, and my party will not join him or his bloc under any circumstances," Bennett said on Saturday.He also called for a "Zionist unity government headed by Eisenkot", arguing that distrust of Netanyahu was justified because he had repeatedly deceived his political partners.Bennett's position comes eventhough he had met Netanyahu earlier in the week, triggering speculation that he could break away from Eisenkot's camp.President Isaac Herzog formally tasked Eisenkot with forming a government on November 8, after consultations with political parties. Factions representing 67 lawmakers recommended Eisenkot for the mandate, compared with 46 who backed Netanyahu. One faction representing seven lawmakers did not recommend either candidate.Under Israeli law, Eisenkot has 28 days from receiving the mandate to form a government. Herzog can grant him an extension of up to 14 additional days if required. This puts the initial deadline in early December, with a possible extension taking the process into the second half of the month.Any proposed government must secure the confidence of the Knesset before taking office. If Eisenkot fails, the process could move to another candidate or another round of political negotiations.
Article Summary: Gadi Eisenkot, the former Israeli military chief tasked with forming the country's next government, has invited Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party for fresh coalition talks. The move could pave the way for a national unity government. The talks are scheduled to begin on Sunday, November 22, as EisenKot faces a December deadline to secure enough support in parliament.

Article Title: IND vs NZ: New Zealand look to Martin Crowe, Brendon McCullum for inspiration as they fight to save Test
Article Text:
Martin Crowe and Brendon McCullum (Image credit: Agencies)

Crowe, McCullum set the benchmark

Conway leads New Zealand's fightback

Pant's century powers India to record total

Bumrah strikes twice, Nicholls falls again

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New Zealand face a huge challenge to save the first Test against India after conceding a 352-run first-innings lead at the Basin Reserve in Wellington. With eight wickets in hand and a minimum of 90 overs left on the final day, the hosts will need a remarkable batting effort to deny India victory. Devon Conway and Rachin Ravindra will have to lead the fightback on Monday. The two left-handers were unbeaten at the close of play on Day 4, with Conway scoring 59 and Ravindra making 27. Their partnership was worth 59 runs as New Zealand reached 119/2 at stumps, still trailing by 233 runs.The task is difficult, but New Zealand can draw inspiration from two famous batting performances at the same venue by Martin Crowe and Brendon McCullum New Zealand have twice produced remarkable batting performances at this venue to save a Test match.The longest they have batted in the third or fourth innings of a Test to save a match was 220.3 overs against Sri Lanka in 1991. They scored 671/4 in that innings. Their second-longest effort came against India in 2014, when they batted for 210 overs and scored 680/8 declared.Both innings featured two of the greatest individual batting performances in New Zealand's Test history. Crowe scored a magnificent 299 against Sri Lanka in 1991, while McCullum made 302 against India in 2014.Conway and Ravindra will need something special of their own if New Zealand are to survive the final day.Conway gave New Zealand some hope with an unbeaten half-century before stumps. He was joined by Ravindra as the hosts tried to recover from India's massive first-innings total of 720/9.India's total was the highest ever by a team in a Test innings in New Zealand. It also put the visitors in a commanding position after the hosts had managed 368 in their first innings.New Zealand still need another 233 runs just to make India bat again, while the visitors have eight wickets to take to seal the match.India's massive total was built on outstanding contributions from their top-order batters.KL Rahul led the way with 136. He added 130 runs for the opening wicket with Yashasvi Jaiswal, who scored 85. Rahul then shared a 165-run stand with Devdutt Padikkal (80) and added another 91 with captain Shubman Gill, who scored 98 before getting out two balls before the end of the third day.Rishabh Pant then took charge with an attacking 128 off 153 balls. He added 100 runs with Gill, 68 with nightwatchman Anshul Kamboj and 75 with Dhruv Jurel, who scored 78.Pant's century was the ninth of his Test career and his fourth since returning to the format in 2024, two years after his serious car accident.Pant said scoring a century in New Zealand was special, as it was a place where he had been keen to reach the milestone.“I think definitely it was a good innings. New Zealand was one place where I was eyeing that century for sure,” Pant said. “In a match like this where everyone has to grind and is batting well I just wanted to stay there as long as possible and make my impact.“I just keep it simple most of the time. Whenever I see the ball I try to hit it.”Pant enjoyed taking on the New Zealand bowlers and fielders, who had five players stationed near the boundary. He used a wide range of shots, including three sixes down the ground, shots behind square and several boundaries on the leg side. He also played his trademark reverse sweep.With Pant and Jurel scoring quickly, India were able to declare their innings midway through the second session. Jurel completed his third Test half-century off 61 balls.Jasprit Bumrah gave India an early breakthrough in New Zealand's second innings by dismissing captain Tom Latham for a duck.Bumrah had also dismissed Latham in the first innings, bowling him with the third ball of New Zealand's innings after beating him with a delivery that moved back in from outside off stump.This time, the India pacer produced a delivery that moved away after pitching. Latham pushed forward tentatively and edged the ball to wicketkeeper Pant.Henry Nicholls, who had scored an unbeaten 175 in the first innings, began New Zealand's second innings with the third ball. He looked comfortable while making 31 but was eventually dismissed by Prasidh Krishna.Nicholls edged Krishna's delivery onto his thigh pad, and the ball popped up for Jurel to take an athletic catch on the leg side.Bumrah returned to bowl the final over of the day with seven fielders on the leg side, but India could not pick up another wicket.With Conway and Ravindra at the crease, New Zealand will need a long and determined effort on the final day to keep the match alive.
Article Summary: New Zealand concede 352-run first-innings lead against India. Hosts need a remarkable batting effort to deny India victory. Devon Conway and Rachin Ravindra will have to lead the fightback. New Zealand have twice produced remarkable batting performances at this venue to save a Test match.

Article Title: India, Malaysia begin Harimau Shakti military drill with focus on counter-terror ops
Article Text:
Indian Army contingent in Malaysia for Exercise Hiramau Shakti. (Image credit: Indian Army)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The sixth edition of the India-Malaysia joint military exercise Harimau Shakti began on Friday at Ipoh in Malaysia, with 120 personnel from each side taking part. The exercise, a bilateral training event held alternately in the two countries, will run till November 30.The stated aim is to rehearse sub-conventional operations under Chapter VII of the United Nations mandate, with particular emphasis on synergising responses during counter-terrorism missions. The two armies will work in jungle and semi-urban terrain, relying on joint planning, tactical coordination and emerging technologies to improve interoperability.The exercise will unfold in phases. In the first phase, troops will first undergo cross-training to familiarise themselves with each other's operating procedures, followed by joint tactical drills. These include setting up a Joint Command Post and Surveillance Centre, counter-terrorism operations, raids, cordon-and-search drills and combat engineering tasks. Special attention will go to Unmanned Aerial Systems for reconnaissance and surveillance, along with counter-drone capabilities to detect and neutralise hostile unmanned platforms. The exercise will end with a validation drill built around a simulated counter-terrorism scenario, combining ground operations, integrated surveillance and unmanned systems.The fifth edition was held last year at the Mahajan Field Firing Range in Rajasthan from December 5 to 18 last year. The Indian contingent then largely comprised troops from the Dogra Regiment, while Malaysia was represented by the 25th Battalion of the Royal Malaysian Army.The exercise reflects a wider deepening of defence ties. India and Malaysia established diplomatic relations in 1957 and a Memorandum of Understanding on Defence Cooperation signed in 1993 gave military engagement an institutional framework. The Joint Defence Cooperation Committee reviews existing cooperation and identifies new areas. In August 2024, the two countries elevated their ties to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.The naval dimension has grown as well. The fourth edition of Samudra Laksamana was held at Lumut from September 9 to 12 this year, with INS Mysore exercising alongside the Royal Malaysian Navy's KD Lekir and KD Gagah Samudera.In October 2025 INS Sahyadri visited Kemaman, while the survey vessel INS Sandhayak made a port call at Klang in July 2025. The navies of both nations also take part in multilateral platforms such as MILAN and the ASEAN-India Maritime Exercise.Defence manufacturing is emerging as another area of cooperation. India is looking to expand exports to Southeast Asia, while Malaysia seeks to modernise its forces and diversify its sources of procurement. Hindustan Aeronautics Limited, Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders, Bharat Dynamics Limited and BEML showcased their products at LIMA 2025. The two countries are also co-chairing the SEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting-Plus (ADMM) counter-terrorism working group for 2024-2027.
Article Summary: The sixth edition of the India-Malaysia joint military exercise Harimau Shakti began on Friday at Ipoh in Malaysia. The exercise, a bilateral training event held alternately in the two countries, will run till November 30. The stated aim is to rehearse sub-conventional operations under Chapter VII of the United Nations mandate.
